errors.text: The proposed high-temperature stacking-fault-energy collapse is contradicted by cited evidence E2, which reports that stacking-fault energy increases with temperature and suppresses stacking faults and nanotwins.
The falsification logic is internally inconsistent: persistence of the friction spike when thermal disorder is suppressed would undermine, not support, a disorder-driven amorphization mechanism.

Mechanical amorphization and enhanced adhesion to the Cu matrix are asserted without system-specific evidence, and low shear strength alone does not explain an increased tangential force or friction coefficient.
